record.question:
A retailer wants to replace its on-premises call-center platform with managed AWS services. It needs inbound calling, contact flows, queues, and agent routing. Callers should also be able to state a request naturally, supply required details, and complete supported tasks without an agent, with context available if transfer is needed.

Which services should form the core of this solution? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon Polly as the sole component for recognizing caller intent and collecting conversational details.
Use Amazon Connect to provide the contact center, telephone numbers, flows, queues, and agent routing.
Use a fixed touch-tone menu as the only automated interaction, with no speech or natural-language intent processing.
Transcribe completed call recordings and analyze the text with Amazon Comprehend after calls end, using that analysis as the self-service interaction.
Integrate an Amazon Lex V2 bot into the contact flow to recognize intent, collect slots, and invoke supported business operations or transfer with context.

explanation.text:
<<2>> and <<5>> are correct. Connect supplies the contact-center workflow and agent handling. Lex provides speech recognition, natural-language understanding, and dialog state so the flow can gather the information needed for a supported task. Fulfillment code can call the retailer's authorized backend operations.

<<1>> turns text into speech, but does not by itself understand the caller's intent or manage the required dialog.

<<3>> can implement useful menu routing, but fails the natural-language interaction requirement.

<<4>> supports retrospective analytics rather than resolving the caller's request during the live conversation.

Configure intents, slots, error handling, fulfillment authorization, and the agent-transfer path. Speech understanding is not caller identity verification, and a bot should authenticate the customer before performing sensitive operations. Use a published Lex V2 version and appropriate alias for production traffic.

AWS documentation (checked September 18, 2026): [Connect and Lex integration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/amazon-lex.html); [Amazon Lex V2 capabilities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lexv2/latest/dg/what-is.html); [Amazon Polly text to speech](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/what-is.html).

diagram_alt: Connect handles the call and agent path, while Lex gathers intent and details for an authorized self-service action.

sources.supports: A Connect flow can integrate a Lex bot for intents, slots, self-service interactions, and transfer to an agent.
Lex V2 provides automatic speech recognition, natural language understanding, dialog management, and business-function integration.
Polly converts text to speech rather than recognizing caller intent.

editorial_notes: Preserved answers 2 and 5. Removed obsolete Alexa for Business and unrelated visual-recognition distractors, and contrasted live conversational fulfillment with valid but insufficient speech output, keypad routing, and post-call analytics.
